steps.body: Money problems are measurement problems with dollars as the unit: nine passes at 25 dollars build 225, and a 40-dollar voucher leaves 185.
steps.narration: Money problems are measurement problems with dollars as the unit: nine passes at 25 dollars build 225, and a 40-dollar voucher leaves 185.

widget.prompt: Build the cost of four passes at 25 dollars each, in dollars.
widget.successFeedback: 100 dollars in four equal parts of 25 — the total before any voucher comes off.
widget.partialFeedback: Every pass costs the same 25 dollars; build each bar to 25.

predict.prompt: Nine passes at 25 dollars, 40 off. Total?
predict.reveal: 225 built, then 40 removed once — a voucher reduces the bill rather than adding to it.

cml.actionGoal: Model equal prices and a single voucher as multiply, then subtract once.
invariants: A voucher reduces the completed total once; it does not reduce every item unless the story says so.
misconceptions: Adding the number of passes to the price or adding the voucher.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A group buys 4 passes at 40 dollars each and a voucher takes 28 dollars off. How many dollars?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the price before the voucher; the discount still has to come off.
A voucher reduces the bill, so the last step subtracts.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Multiply to build the equal-group total, then subtract the one stated adjustment.

widget.prompt: Apply the money model: which expression finds the cost of 6 passes at 25 dollars after one 20-dollar voucher?

options.label: (6 × 25) − 20 = 130 dollars
options.feedback: Correct — equal prices build 150 dollars, then the one voucher removes 20 dollars.

options.label: 6 × (25 − 20) = 30 dollars
options.feedback: That applies the one voucher to every pass instead of once to the total.

options.label: 6 + 25 − 20 = 11 dollars
options.feedback: Six counts passes and 25 is dollars per pass; equal groups require multiplication.

options.label: (6 × 25) + 20 = 170 dollars
options.feedback: A voucher reduces the bill, so the final operation is subtraction.
